clue.text: British Power introducing complete copper plant

indicators.note: the British-and-Power pair is introducing the other pieces into its middle, so they sit between B and P

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
complete, as in 'a complete fool', means utter
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A British energy company brings in copper wholesale to build a power plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like an industrial site in a story about power and copper, but it is a flower. 'Introducing' means the British-and-Power pair takes the rest inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow wild flower, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Fawlty in charge of a building in Rome

parts.note: Basil Fawlty is the hotelier in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers

explanation.surface: Basil Fawlty, the sitcom hotel owner, is put in charge of a Roman building.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a 1970s BBC comedy set in a seaside hotel run by the rude Basil Fawlty.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large church of a style found in ancient and modern Rome, such as St Peter's.

clue.text: Charge of cab not going all the way

indicators.note: a cab ride that stops short of its destination; here the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Talk of a taxi fare for a ride that stopped before reaching its destination.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax is a charge levied by government on income or goods.

clue.text: Everton's first opening game?

indicators.note: the first letter of Everton is taken, the possessive showing it belongs to that word

parts.note: a vent is an opening that lets air or gas out

explanation.surface: A question about whether Everton, the football club, played the season's opening match.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is an English Premier League football club from Liverpool. The question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting event can be a single game or match, so the definition is an example with a question mark.

clue.text: Tory going down as offensively patronising

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party
going down means descending

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician loses favour by acting in a superior, patronising way.
explanation.definitionFit: Condescending describes someone treating others as inferior, a sneering superiority that gives offence.

clue.text: Selection of food — continuous talk about pounds

indicators.note: the talk is placed about, that is around, the abbreviation for pounds

parts.note: patter is rapid continuous talk, as from a salesman
L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A waiter's endless spiel about the price of a food selection.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter is an assortment of food served on a large plate, such as a cheese platter.

clue.text: Parental guidance needed about current nature of Peppa

indicators.note: the certificate letters go about, or around, the symbol for current

parts.note: PG is the film certificate for parental guidance
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Parents are advised to watch with their children what a cartoon character is really like.
explanation.walkthrough: Peppa Pig is a British children's cartoon about a little pig.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon character Peppa is an animal of this kind, so the clue asks what kind of creature she is.

clue.text: Sue creeps out all over the place

indicators.note: letters scattered all over the place are in disorder and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman called Sue gets the creeps and is in a terrible state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a woman's name, but it is the verb meaning take legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue someone is to bring legal proceedings against them, which is what a prosecutor does in court.

clue.text: Size of crowd entering at Everton needs greatly reducing

indicators.note: the phrase entering at Everton needs to be cut down a great deal, leaving only a few letters from its middle

explanation.surface: A football crowd coming into the Everton ground is so large that it must be cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across enterinG AT Everton. In football the gate is the number of people at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate in sport is the attendance at a match, counted as spectators pass through the turnstiles.

clue.text: 4 x 4 exits badly with men missing motorway

indicators.note: exits written badly are put in the wrong order
the men are missing the abbreviation for motorway

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A four-by-four vehicle leaves the motorway badly, with workers missing.
explanation.walkthrough: '4 x 4' looks like an off-road car but is the sum four times four. SIXTE is EXITS rearranged; MEN without M is EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Four multiplied by four makes sixteen, so the arithmetic is the definition.

clue.text: An attack of illness is concerning

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A
a bout is a spell or attack of illness, as in a bout of flu

explanation.surface: A bout of sickness is worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concerning' reads as worrying, but it means on the subject of.
explanation.definitionFit: About and concerning are synonyms meaning on the subject of or regarding.

clue.text: Minimum as written into lease

indicators.note: as is written into the word, the way a clause is written into a contract

parts.note: to let is to lease property

explanation.surface: A minimum clause that has been written into a tenancy agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The least is the smallest amount possible, which is a minimum.

clue.text: Praise a key speech

parts.note: D is a musical key
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Praise for a speech that was central to an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective meaning important, but it is a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and worship, giving devoted praise to someone.

clue.text: The one or the other unit covered in solvent

indicators.note: the unit is covered in the solvent, which wraps around it

parts.note: ether is an organic liquid used as a solvent
I, the Roman numeral for one, stands for a unit

explanation.surface: One part or another of a factory unit has been covered in solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: Either refers to one or the other of two things, whichever is chosen.

clue.text: Put one's foot down hard over European charge

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, or above, the second

parts.note: to put one's foot down hard is to stamp; the past tense is stamped

explanation.surface: Someone firmly refuses to pay a European fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot down' suggests a firm refusal and 'charge' a fee, but the foot really stamps and the charge is a headlong rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden mass charge of animals or people rushing in panic.

clue.text: Fail to win in record lap in local relay

indicators.note: the losing word goes in the record's letters

parts.note: CD, compact disc, is a record
to fail to win is to lose
a lap is a circuit of a track

explanation.surface: A team misses out on a record time on a lap of a local relay race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relay' suggests a race, but here it means broadcast: closed-circuit TV relays pictures to a limited local set of screens.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed-circuit system transmits pictures only to a restricted set of monitors, a broadcast confined to one place.

clue.text: Ruler's uncontrolled anger beheaded men

indicators.note: the word for anger loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: temper is an outburst of uncontrolled anger
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers, the men

explanation.surface: A tyrant flies into a rage and has men beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the supreme sovereign of an empire, so a monarch or ruler.

clue.text: Mother swan's wet

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A mother swan is wet from swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: A female swan is a pen and a male is a cob.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen is to make something slightly wet or moist, so the verb fits.

clue.text: Best prepare for exam about English

indicators.note: the study word wraps about the abbreviation for English

parts.note: to cram is to study hard at the last minute before an exam

explanation.surface: Advice that the best way to revise for an English exam is to start early.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, the elite, as cream rises to the top of milk.

clue.text: Friend in the country

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so ... means a friend
second meaning: the large East Asian nation

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang shortens a rhyming phrase: china plate rhymes with mate, and only the first word is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is London slang for a pal and also the name of the most populous East Asian nation.

clue.text: Notice heads up

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: the tops of things are their heads

explanation.surface: A warning that someone should look out: heads up!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads up' looks like a warning cry but is the word for the tops of things, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it, to notice it.

clue.text: Abbot's deputy with previous conviction

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the monk ranking just below the abbot in an abbey
second meaning: in slang a ... is a criminal record entry from before

explanation.surface: A monastery's second-in-command turns out to have a criminal record.
explanation.definitionFit: The monastic officer below an abbot holds this title, and police slang uses the same word for an earlier criminal record.

clue.text: Do an impression of one friend with grasp of Italian

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the friend holds, or has a grasp of, the abbreviation for Italian

parts.note: a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone mimics a friend who speaks good Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to copy or mimic someone, which is what an impressionist does.

clue.text: A party in difficulty

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A party that has run into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or trouble, as in 'without further ado', so it is a kind of bother or difficulty.

clue.text: Weight's never going over

indicators.note: the word turns over, so its letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: never means not at any time, so not

explanation.surface: A boast that a weight will never tip over.
explanation.definitionFit: A ton is a unit of weight, about a thousand kilograms.

clue.text: Fix mother part in long rambling story

parts.note: to rig is to fix a result dishonestly
ma is an informal word for mother
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A mother is cast in a part in a long, rambling tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a lengthy, confused account or a long-winded and complicated procedure.
